# Fixture provenance

- Run `python3 tests/fixtures/generate.py` to regenerate the Python-produced ZIP, ZIP64, TAR, GZIP, XZ and BZIP2 fixtures and refresh the unencrypted Swift resources.
- `sample.7z` was created using 7-Zip with `-t7z -m0=LZMA2 -mhc=off` from `notes.txt` containing the fixture message. The LZ4 and Zstandard files are CLI-compressed versions of the same message and `sample.tar`.
- `test_read_format_rar.rar` and `test_read_format_rar5_stored.rar` are decoded .uu fixtures from [libarchive v3.8.11](https://github.com/libarchive/libarchive/tree/v3.8.11/libarchive/test). See the [upstream license notices](../../third_party/libarchive.txt).
- `zipcrypto.zip` and `aes256.zip` contain `public.txt` with `Public document\n` and `private.txt` with `Protected document\n`. The public file was added without encryption. The protected file was added using Info-ZIP `-P fixture-pass` and 7-Zip `-tzip -mem=AES256 -pfixture-pass` respectively. The Swift test resources use copies of the same fixtures.
- `sample.iso` was created with `bsdtar --format=iso9660` from the fixture `notes.txt`.
- `test_read_format_cab_2.cab`, `test_read_format_cab_3.cab`, and `test_read_format_lha_lh7.lzh` are decoded normal-format .uu fixtures from [libarchive v3.8.11](https://github.com/libarchive/libarchive/tree/v3.8.11/libarchive/test), covering MSZIP, LZX, and LH7. See the [upstream license notices](../../third_party/libarchive.txt).
- `notes.br`, `empty.br`, and `expansion.br` were created with the Brotli CLI from the fixture message, empty input, and 220,000 bytes of ASCII `x`, respectively.
- `volumes/` contains three parts each of ZIP and 7z made with 7-Zip `-v64b`. The 7z set uses LZMA2. Both contain `notes.txt` with `Known bytes for volume validation.\n`. The Swift test resources use copies of the same parts.
- `independent/disk.*` was created with Info-ZIP `zip -0 -s 64k` using a 135,680-byte repeated byte pattern and a short text file. `small-disk64.*` is generated by `generate.py` with ZIP64 disk-relative offsets and central directory records on two disks.
- `independent/old.part*.rar` and `independent/new.part*.rar` are decoded upstream `test_rar_multivolume_single_file` and `test_read_format_rar5_multiarchive_solid` fixtures from libarchive v3.8.11. The Swift test resources reuse these inputs and the small disk ZIP64.
- `members.gz` concatenates two valid members. `gzip-crc.gz` and `gzip-size.gz` contain a multi-block stream with one modified trailer field each.
- `prefixed-zip.bin` prepends an inert header to the standard ZIP fixture to exercise central-directory recognition without a ZIP extension.
- `profile-box.bin` contains a fixed header, the standard ZIP and an unrelated footer. `format-profile.json` bounds the ZIP payload and verifies the header signature.
- `resource-index.zip` contains explicit and implicit directories, paths that normalize to the same name, a UTF-8 file, a path outside the resource namespace, and a file that conflicts with directory traversal.
- `composition-patch.zip` provides replacement content and a file whose name collides with an implicit directory in `nested.zip`.
- `nested.zip` contains a ZIP named `packages/内层.bin`. That archive in turn contains the standard `sample.zip` fixture under the name `deep.zip`.
- `sample.xp3` and the XP3 edge case fixtures come from `generate.py`. The valid sample has a chained raw and compressed index, a UTF-16LE path, an empty file, and a file split into stored and zlib segments.
- `xp3-wrapped.bin` places a standard raw XP3 after an inert aligned MZ prefix to test detection and offsets without executable code.
- `xp3-upstream.xp3` was packed with [KiriKiri Z Web's xp3pack.py](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_web/blob/2fe46168acebc9ecf093d95e630a98f50a17efba/tools/xp3pack.py). The source files are `notes.txt` containing the fixture message and `docs/样本.txt` containing 12,000 copies of `XP3 resource line\n`.
